notes: The substrate contains explicit chapter numerals at intervals (ⲋ̄=6, ⲍ̄=7, ⲓ̄ⲅ=13, ⲓ̄ⲑ=19, ⲕ̄ⲁ=21, ⲕ̄ⲉ=25, ⲕ̄ⲋ=26, ⲗⲑ=39, ⲝ̄=60, ⲟⲁ=71, ⲟⲇ=74, ϥ̄ⲏ=98, ⲣⲇ̄=104, ⲣⲋ=106, ⲣⲍ=107, ⲣⲏ=108, ⲣⲓⲁ=111), confirming this is a Kephalaia tradition with at least 111+ chapters. Many boundaries in the heavily lacunose middle sections (between explicit chapter numbers) are determined by topical shifts and the recurring formula 'ⲉⲧⲃⲉ' (Concerning...). Several boundaries in §§778-1130 are uncertain due to the fragmentary nature of those folios. The chapters between ⲣⲓⲁ (§5394) and the end may include several more topical units that I have grouped conservatively. Sections §1916-2240 are densely populated with sub-mappings (Five Things in Body, Ten Things, etc.) which I treat as separate teaching units following the 'mapping one subject' criterion. The opening (§1-21) is too fragmentary to securely identify as a distinct chapter — it may be the conclusion of a prior teaching about the Good Tree.
